clue.text: Superman's from Brum: hence Lois's terminal dithering

definitions.note: read as 'Superman is', the 's standing for is before the wordplay

indicators.note: dithering is shaky, unsettled movement, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: terminal means the end, so take only the last letter of the word Lois's

explanation.surface: A Birmingham-born superhero whose arrival leaves his girlfriend Lois dithering to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brum' is a nickname for Birmingham, and the setter is Brummie, but here it is just fodder. 'dithering' jumbles BRUM, HENCE and S (the last letter of Lois's, from 'terminal').
explanation.definitionFit: Nietzsche's term for the superior human is usually translated into English as Superman.

clue.text: Daniel's mate sleeping at Newcastle region game

parts.note: abed means in bed, sleeping
Newcastle is in north-east England, abbreviated NE
a go is a turn in a game, or the board game Go

explanation.surface: A friend of Daniel's dozing at a match in the north-east.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Daniel, Abednego is one of Daniel's three companions thrown into the fiery furnace.

clue.text: Sensitive Tynan's missing relative with that hurt inside

indicators.note: inside places the cry of pain within what remains of the name
missing means the relative's letters are dropped from the name

parts.note: Kenneth Tynan, the theatre critic
a nan is a grandmother, a relative
ouch is what one says when something hurts

explanation.surface: A thin-skinned critic whose missing relative leaves him wounded within.
explanation.walkthrough: Kenneth Tynan was a famous British theatre critic; 'missing' and 'inside' work in turn, the first cutting a grandmother out of his name, the second planting a cry of pain in what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchy person is easily offended, quick to take things personally.

clue.text: Miss having new top and bunting

indicators.note: a new top means the first letter of the word is changed for another

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A young woman wears a new blouse and decorates with flags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having new top' swaps the G at the head of GIRL; the clue does not say which letter replaces it, so the bird's name must supply C. 'bunting' looks like flags but is a family of songbirds.
explanation.definitionFit: The cirl is a species of bunting, a small seed-eating songbird found in south-west England.

clue.text: Lessons to be learnt when Carreras and chums lose 10-0

indicators.note: to lose is to give up, so these letters are taken away from the group's name

parts.note: José Carreras, Plácido Domingo and Luciano Pavarotti sang as the Three Tenors
10 is TEN and 0 is the letter O, a scoreline written out

explanation.surface: The famous opera trio suffer a ten-nil thrashing and learn a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose' takes TEN and O from the middle of THE THREE TENORS. The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading, writing and arithmetic are the basic lessons of schooling, each said with an R sound.

clue.text: Loudmouth Simpson's without Josh — good

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the cartoon name goes round

parts.note: Bart Simpson of the cartoon The Simpsons
to josh is to tease, as is to rag

explanation.surface: A loud character from The Simpsons is better off without his friend Josh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking. 'Josh' looks like a person's name but is the verb meaning to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A braggart is a boaster, someone who talks loudly about himself.

clue.text: Develop gun (repeating) right away

indicators.note: away means the doubled letter is taken out of the weapon

parts.note: a revolver is a handgun

indicators.note: repeating means the abbreviation is used twice over

explanation.surface: Develop a repeating gun and do away with the right to bear it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeating' doubles R for right, and 'away' removes both Rs from REVOLVER. A repeating gun is a real kind of firearm, which disguises the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve is to develop gradually over time.

clue.text: Advantage of puzzle lacking number and name

indicators.note: lacking means the following abbreviations are taken out of the verb

parts.note: to nonplus is to puzzle or perplex

explanation.surface: The benefit of a crossword that has no numbers or names in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puzzle' is a verb here, not a crossword: NONPLUS loses NO and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is a positive feature or benefit, an advantage.

clue.text: As a primate gives blessing to one during party

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so these letters sit inside the party

parts.note: a bash is a party
a boon is a blessing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone at a party gives a blessing to one guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is the container signal; 'gives' and 'to' only link the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Baboonish describes behaviour like that of a baboon, a large monkey and so a primate.

clue.text: Get knotted, scorer!

definitions.meaning: one who writes musical scores: Maurice, the French composer of Boléro

explanation.surface: Someone tells a goal-scorer, rudely, to get lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get knotted' is British slang for go away, but here it means become tangled; the scorer is a composer, not a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravel can mean to tangle, and Maurice Ravel was a French composer, someone who wrote scores.

clue.text: Having spokes injected with carbon is basic

indicators.note: injected with means a substance is put inside, so the element's symbol goes in

parts.note: radial means arranged like spokes from a centre
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A wheel with spokes treated with carbon is a fundamental design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injected with' puts C inside RADIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical means going to the root of something, so fundamental or basic.

clue.text: Switches between kind of shirt and topless swimwear

parts.note: a T-shirt, so the letter T

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed from the word

parts.note: goggles are worn by swimmers

explanation.surface: Someone alternates between a shirt and nothing above the waist at the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the G from the front of GOGGLES; 'topless swimwear' suggests a bikini bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Toggles are switches that flip between two positions.

clue.text: Reflective lines, say, in city

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation sits inside the city's name

parts.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
e.g., for example, means say

explanation.surface: Thoughtful verses composed, for example, in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; the city is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful, reflective poem, so its lines are reflective.

clue.text: Mini modified genera of seaweed

parts.note: the Mini is a famous small car

indicators.note: modified means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small car customised with different kinds of seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mini' looks like an adjective for a small seaweed, but it is the British car; 'modified' is the anagram signal for the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrageen is an edible red seaweed, also called Irish moss.

clue.text: McBain enters Leicester High, fed up

annotationWithheld.why: McBain enters Leicester High, fed up (7,3): ED (McBain) in CHEESE (Leicester) plus OFF (High) gives eleven letters, CHEESEDEOFF, one E too many; no reading of the clue as held gives CHEESEDOFF

clue.text: Interested party prone to tangle with Krays

indicators.note: to tangle with is to mix things up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tempted to pick a fight with the notorious London gangsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangle with' jumbles PRONE and KRAYS; the Krays were twin gangsters in 1960s London.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosy parker is a busybody who takes too close an interest in other people's affairs.

clue.text: High Street employees after those lifting items?

definitions.text: High Street employees after those lifting items?

parts.words: High Street employees after those lifting items?
parts.note: lifting suggests weightlifters but means shoplifters, whom shop staff pursue

explanation.surface: Shop workers chase people carrying goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Store detectives are staff employed by shops to catch shoplifters.

clue.text: National schoolboy gobbling seconds

indicators.note: gobbling means swallowing, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil at Eton College

explanation.surface: A schoolboy wolfing down second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gobbling' puts S inside ETONIAN; Eton is England's famous boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: An Estonian is a national, a citizen, of Estonia.

clue.text: Estate agents' examinations

parts.note: examinations suggests tests sat by estate agents, but means house inspections they arrange for buyers

explanation.definitionFit: Viewings are visits arranged by estate agents so buyers can inspect a property.

clue.text: Repulsive pants and saintly features restrict sex lives

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so these letters go round the next

parts.note: saints are shown with halos
it is a slang word for sex appeal or sex
is means exists, lives

explanation.surface: Unpleasant underwear and holy images curb people's sex lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' means breaths, not underwear. 'restrict' is the container signal, and 'sex lives' splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Halitosis is bad breath, so its pants, or breaths, are repulsive.

clue.text: One's no right to go in off them

definitions.text: One's no right to go in off them

parts.words: One's no right to go in off them
parts.note: an area declared off something is one nobody may enter

explanation.definitionFit: A place off limits is forbidden territory, somewhere one may not enter.

clue.text: Leading United and excited

parts.note: united means made one
up means excited, as in worked up

explanation.surface: Manchester United in front and thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club but means as one.
explanation.definitionFit: To be one up is to be ahead by one, leading.

clue.text: Legendary bard, Ms Phillips, goes after map makers

indicators.note: goes after means this name follows the abbreviation

parts.note: OS is the Ordnance Survey, Britain's official mapmaker
Siân Phillips, the Welsh actress

explanation.surface: A Welsh actress pursues cartographers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes after' fixes the order; the map makers are the Ordnance Survey, Britain's national mapping agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossian was the legendary Gaelic bard whose poems Macpherson claimed to translate.

clue.text: King Edward exploited having the royal habit

parts.note: ER, Edwardus Rex, is King Edward's royal cipher
mined means exploited, as a resource

explanation.surface: A king exploited his subjects in his regal clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Edward' suggests the potato, but ER is the royal cipher, Latin for King Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermined means trimmed with ermine, the fur of royal robes, so dressed in the royal habit or garb.

clue.text: Public showing of Blake's final version of "Windows with Duck"

indicators.note: final means only the last letter of the poet's name is taken

parts.note: Windows XP was a version of Microsoft's operating system
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: An exhibition of Blake's last painting, of a window and a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' tells you XP is one release of Windows; O is a duck, the cricket score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is an exposition, a large public exhibition.

clue.text: One getting into old film star's bodice

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so the numeral goes inside the name

parts.note: Buster Keaton, the silent film comedian
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone squeezing into a vintage film star's corset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into' puts I inside BUSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustier is a tight, strapless bodice.

clue.text: Plump knight's gone thin

indicators.note: gone means the chess letter has departed from the word

parts.note: bonny can mean healthy-looking or plump
N is the knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A plump knight has slimmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' removes N from BONNY.
explanation.definitionFit: Bony means skinny, so thin that the bones show.

clue.text: PM Blair's heart shaped bread

parts.note: William Pitt, British prime minister

indicators.note: heart means the central letter of the name

explanation.surface: Tony Blair's heart-shaped bread.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'heart-shaped', but 'heart' takes the middle letter A of BLAIR; the PM is not Blair but Pitt.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, oval Middle Eastern bread, a shaped bread.

clue.text: Cooler to swing? Nonsense!

parts.note: a fan cools the air
to dangle is to hang and swing

explanation.surface: A fan sways, which is ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: Fandangle means ridiculous ornament or nonsense.
